It builds traced test scripts, a UAT tracker, defect log and a go/no-go pack whose counts a script recomputes; humans execute tests, triage and decide, and the decision block stays empty.
uat-validation.requires: The requirements workbook with requirement IDs, the Test Plan and the SOW acceptance section, plus Python 3 for the traceability gate.

usability-testing.what: Plan usability research or synthesize observations.
usability-testing.when: A team needs participant tasks, sessions, or findings.
usability-testing.inputs: The research questions, interface, participant context, and supplied observations.
usability-testing.outputs: A session plan, neutral task scripts, or supported usability findings.
usability-testing.example: Write neutral participant tasks for these research questions and this interface.
usability-testing.expect: It starts from the decision the research should inform, then writes a session plan with neutral task wording or synthesizes the observations you supply. It keeps what participants said, what was observed and interpretation separate, and returns a plan or labeled provisional findings rather than inventing participants, quotes or success rates.

writing-integrity.what: Review prose for clarity, meaning, and the intended voice.
writing-integrity.when: Writing needs drafting, revision, review, or a retained correction.
writing-integrity.inputs: The brief or draft, controlling sources, and an authorized profile when available.
writing-integrity.outputs: Complete reviewed prose and, when enabled, private correction-learning records.
writing-integrity.example: Review this draft for clarity, repetition, and unsupported claims. Preserve its meaning and intended voice; return the complete revision.
writing-integrity.expect: It reviews your text for meaning, structure and sentence patterns, returns complete edits, and keeps quotations, figures and executable syntax exact. Learned preferences are loaded and saved only from a private profile store you have authorized, and it reports a saved correction only when it has a storage receipt.

writing-style-builder.what: Build or revise a person’s private writing profile.
writing-style-builder.when: Someone authorizes a profile from their writing samples.
writing-style-builder.inputs: Authorized samples, the intended author, profile scope, and confirmation.
writing-style-builder.outputs: A reviewed private profile with supported style rules and update controls.
writing-style-builder.example: Build a draft style profile from these authorized samples and identify the rules I need to confirm.
writing-style-builder.expect: It asks whose voice, from which sources and for what purpose, and stops without that authorization even if a mail or chat connector is available. It uses only material the person wrote, shows the proposed profile for confirmation before saving it, and declines to build one when the evidence is too thin.
writing-style-builder.requires: Explicit authorization from the person being profiled and material they supply or authorize; Python 3 runs the profile builder.

tracker-intake.what: Turn a tracker export into canonical tickets, an intake record and a delta.
tracker-intake.when: A new Jira or other tracker export arrives and later work needs to know what changed.
tracker-intake.inputs: The export file or connector tickets, the engagement site.json, and who supplied the export and what it covers.
tracker-intake.outputs: tickets.json, delta.json and an intake-log.json record with hash, origin, scope, redactions and conflicts.
tracker-intake.example: Here is this week's Jira export; record it and tell me what changed since last Tuesday.
tracker-intake.expect: It asks for the export plus who supplied it and what it covers, then converts it to canonical tickets and a delta against the previous export. It reports counts and every conflict such as an unknown status, drops comments and assignees, and does not change tickets in the tracker.
tracker-intake.requires: Python 3, a tracker export (Jira CSV, table CSV or JSON), and the engagement's site.json config.

moscow-story-map.what: Keep a MoSCoW story map whose statuses, estimates and readiness come from the tracker.
moscow-story-map.when: A release backlog needs classing, a readiness view or a critical path, or new tickets need mapping after an export.
moscow-story-map.inputs: content/stories.json, canonical tickets and, after an export, delta.json.
moscow-story-map.outputs: A summary with readiness, Must share, unclassed tickets and the critical path, plus a review queue and class-review exports.
moscow-story-map.example: Which Must stories are not ready to build, and what blocks them?
moscow-story-map.expect: It reads the release's tickets and the client's workflow steps, asks you to supply the client's own class definitions, and writes the judgment fields of the story map. A script then computes readiness, Must share, unclassed tickets and the critical path from the tracker export, and class changes go through review instead of silent edits.
moscow-story-map.requires: Needs an engagement project folder with tracker/tickets.json from a tracker export, config/site.json holding the client's class definitions, and Python 3.

decision-register.what: Keep refinement questions with owners, statuses and answers, and export them for the tracker.
decision-register.when: Refinement or discovery produced open questions that need owners, answers and a record.
decision-register.inputs: content/questions.json and, for exports, the answers saved on the published page.
decision-register.outputs: A checked register, decisions.csv for tracker import and a decision log in Markdown.
decision-register.example: Add the questions from today's refinement notes and list the ones with no owner.
decision-register.expect: It turns questions from your meeting notes or refinement sources into register entries grouped by epic, with a status and an owner only when the sources name one. It reports unknown groups and questions without an owner, and it asks before writing anything to a tracker.
decision-register.requires: Needs the project's content folder with the questions file, the published Decisions page for saved answers, and python3.

review-site.what: Build or refresh a multi-page release review site from tracker exports and content files.
review-site.when: A client team reviews a release backlog with MoSCoW classes, open decisions, workflows and build steps.
review-site.inputs: An engagement folder with site.json, content files and tracker exports, plus the brand profile when one is confirmed.
review-site.outputs: A gated, rendered site published as a private artifact, comment replies, and CSV exports for the tracker.
review-site.example: Refresh the review site with the new Jira export and republish it.
review-site.expect: It builds or refreshes a multi-page review site from a tracker export and content files in an engagement folder. Gates check references, data and writing and a failing writing gate blocks publishing; after they pass you are expected to read each page, and publishing needs a live-artifact check so another writer's changes are not overwritten.
review-site.requires: Needs an engagement folder with a tracker export and Python 3; browser checks need Playwright's Chromium, and publishing needs the artifact tools with the shared database capability.

review-site-kit.what: Shared runtime for the review-site skills: data contract, calculations, page templates and gates.
review-site-kit.when: One of the review-site skills runs; it is not selected on its own.
review-site-kit.inputs: Engagement config, content files and canonical tickets passed by the calling skill.
review-site-kit.outputs: Computed page data, the rendered site and gate results.
review-site-kit.example: Loaded by review-site when it renders and checks the site.
review-site-kit.expect: It is an internal runtime used by the review-site skills and has no entrypoint of its own, so you reach it through tracker-intake, moscow-story-map, decision-register or review-site. Page and rule changes are made in its source templates, never in a rendered output folder.
review-site-kit.requires: Needs Python 3 for its library, and Node.js with Playwright for the browser checks.

workflows.title: Build test cases from tracker tickets
workflows.when: You have a Jira or other tracker export as a CSV and need test scripts traced to requirements.

steps.give: The tracker CSV, the project's config/site.json, and who supplied the export and what it covers.
steps.get: tickets.json, delta.json and intake-log.json, plus a count of added, removed and changed tickets.

steps.give: The tickets as source material. Confirm the epic and story hierarchy it proposes.
steps.get: A two-tab Excel workbook with requirement IDs, user stories, Gherkin acceptance criteria and MoSCoW priorities.

steps.give: The requirements workbook, plus the Test Plan and the SOW acceptance section when you have them.
steps.get: Markdown test scripts traced to requirement IDs, and CSV files for the UAT tracker, defect log and coverage gaps.

workflows.note: UAT validation stops when no requirements workbook exists, so the workbook step comes first. Its coverage check fails the run when a requirement has no test script.

workflows.title: Prepare for a sales call and record what you learned
workflows.when: A call with a prospect is coming up, or one just finished and the notes need a home.

steps.give: What you know about the account, who is attending, the pursuit so far and the decision the call should move.
steps.get: A Markdown call brief with ranked questions, an agenda and recommended next calls.

steps.give: The pursuit record and your notes or transcript from the call.
steps.get: A sourced discovery ledger and the open questions ranked by what they unblock.

steps.give: The offering catalog's qualifier files and the findings from discovery.
steps.get: The best-fitting offerings ranked, with the evidence behind each score and any disqualifier.

workflows.note: Call prep plans the call; discovery brief owns the record after it. Use discovery synthesis instead when the material is research interviews rather than a sales pursuit.

workflows.title: Turn interviews or meeting transcripts into findings
workflows.when: You have transcripts or notes from customer or user conversations and need to know what they say.

steps.give: The transcripts or notes, who attended on each side and the purpose of the research.
steps.get: A summary, job statements, pain points with severity, exact quotes and open questions, in chat and as a Markdown file.

steps.give: The findings about recent struggling moments and switch decisions.
steps.get: Job statements with evidence references, the decisions they change and the research still needed.

steps.give: The touchpoints, roles, friction and systems the research describes.
steps.get: A journey, service blueprint and opportunity map as an HTML page or Markdown, with hypotheses labeled.

workflows.note: Each step quotes or cites its sources. Where the research is missing, the skills label hypotheses and suggest interview prompts instead of inventing evidence.

workflows.title: Estimate, price and propose a scope
workflows.when: A client needs to see what the work includes, what it costs and what they are agreeing to.

steps.give: The scope you have so far, comparable projects, assumptions and rates.
steps.get: An early estimate range with the calculation shown and the conditions that would reopen it.

steps.give: The brief, the scope model, comparables, the rate card and constraints.
steps.get: Scope items and estimates as JSON and a readable Markdown estimate. Unknown effort stays marked as unestimated.

steps.give: The versioned scope, options, assumptions and confirmed prices.
steps.get: A single-file HTML proposal where the client switches between options and the figures reconcile to the quote.

steps.give: The quote, the margin floor and approval ladder, and the delivery lead's sign-off.
steps.get: A review packet with recomputed margin, flagged risks and a figure tie-out against the quote.

steps.give: The confirmed quote model and the approved contract and brand profiles.
steps.get: A Word statement of work checked against the scope and terms.

steps.give: The draft SOW, the confirmed scope and estimate, and the controlling terms.
steps.get: Findings or revisions for ambiguity, repeated clauses and scope mismatches. Price stays unchanged.

workflows.note: Use scope reference instead of the interactive proposal when the client needs a static side-by-side comparison.

workflows.title: Start and run a signed engagement
workflows.when: A deal has signed and the delivery team is taking over.

steps.give: The signed agreement, the quote, the deal record and who is receiving the work.
steps.get: A handoff package that names owners, assumptions and what the client was promised.

steps.give: The accepted handoff, the signed SOW and the delivery model.
steps.get: A draft charter, RAID and decision logs, internal and client kickoff decks, and a Sprint 0 plan.

steps.give: This period's meeting transcripts, the RAID and decision logs, the SOW baseline and time spent.
steps.get: A Markdown status report, new log entries with stable IDs and change-order candidates.

steps.give: The signed scope, release evidence, owners and the go or no-go decision.
steps.get: A cutover runbook, acceptance record, hypercare plan and closeout notes.

workflows.note: Testing between status and cutover follows the test-case workflow. Delivery suite tracks which stage the engagement is in.

workflows.title: Turn requirements into a sprint plan
workflows.when: The team has a requirements workbook and needs to decide what goes into the next sprint.

steps.give: The brief, SOW, transcripts or product sources.
steps.get: A two-tab Excel workbook of epics, stories, Gherkin acceptance criteria and MoSCoW priorities.

steps.give: The workbook's Requirements tab, team estimates, the RAID log and the definition of ready.
steps.get: A readiness report marking each item READY, REFINE or DISCOVERY, with proposed splits.

steps.give: The candidate items, their scores and where each score came from.
steps.get: A ranked list with each item's formula, unsourced scores flagged and the person who decides named.

steps.give: Who is available, the readiness report, the RAID log and recent velocity.
steps.get: A sprint plan with a goal, per-person capacity, committed and stretch work, and a check that fails when commitment exceeds capacity.

workflows.note: Prioritization proposes a ranking; the Product Owner or client decides it.

workflows.title: Review a release backlog with the client
workflows.when: The client needs to review stories, priorities and open decisions on one shared page.

steps.give: The latest tracker export and the project's config/site.json.
steps.get: tickets.json and a delta of what changed since the last export.

steps.give: The tickets and the client's workflow steps and MoSCoW classes.
steps.get: A story map with readiness, Must share and critical path, a review queue in Markdown and CSV class reviews.

steps.give: The open questions from refinement notes, ticket comments or meetings.
steps.get: A checked question register, decisions.csv for the tracker and a Markdown decision log.

steps.give: The project folder with site.json, the story map, the questions and the brand profile.
steps.get: A private review site where the client answers questions and reviews classes, plus CSV exports.

workflows.note: Rerun tracker intake after each new export; the review site refresh reads its delta.

workflows.title: Build a client deck from your evidence
workflows.when: You need slides that make a case to a specific audience and decision.

steps.give: The project sources and the claims the deck will make.
steps.get: A source register, the claims split into checkable statements and a decision on whether the evidence is enough.

steps.give: The audience, the decision, the evidence and the output format.
steps.get: An editable PowerPoint or HTML deck with reviewed copy and rendered checks.

steps.give: The finished deck, its sources and the checks already run.
steps.get: A release decision with findings and required repairs.

workflows.note: For a deck where the client chooses between scoped options, use the deal decision deck instead of deck builder.

workflows.title: Define a product change from evidence
workflows.when: A product needs its next change defined from what users need.

steps.give: The product brief, current sources, decisions and readiness evidence.
steps.get: An updated product record and the next supported step.

steps.give: The research transcripts or notes and their purpose.
steps.get: Findings with exact quotes, pain points and open questions.

steps.give: The touchpoints, roles and friction from the research.
steps.get: A journey, service blueprint and opportunity map.

steps.give: The current implementation, user flows, interfaces, data and constraints.
steps.get: A specification with UI states, data, interfaces and acceptance checks, as Markdown or HTML.

steps.give: The research questions, the interface and who the participants are.
steps.get: A session plan with neutral task scripts, or findings from sessions you ran.

workflows.note: The product pathway picks the next step from the product's readiness evidence.

workflows.title: Prepare a career application
workflows.when: You are assessing a role and preparing the materials to apply.

steps.give: The posting, your career sources and the role work record.
steps.get: A role assessment and a role-specific resume copy as a Word document.

steps.give: Your career evidence, the posting and the draft resume.
steps.get: Revised resume bullets with figures and posting keywords that keep your stated scope.

steps.give: The role record, your career evidence and who the material is for.
steps.get: Drafts such as a cover letter, LinkedIn copy or reference list.

steps.give: The role or offer terms and your criteria.
steps.get: An offer comparison, open questions and negotiation drafts for your decision.

workflows.note: These workflows are in the estate-personal plugin. Career application never submits a form without your explicit go-ahead.

workflows.title: Create and maintain a skill
workflows.when: A task you repeat should become a skill, or an existing skill needs a change.

steps.give: The recurring task, example requests, the method and good outputs.
steps.get: The skill folder with its SKILL.md, resources and validation evidence.

steps.give: The new or changed skill and its test outputs.
steps.get: A release decision with required repairs.

steps.give: The Skills Estate checkout and the reviewed source hash.
steps.get: Validation results, built packages and install receipts.

workflows.note: A repository merge, a local install and an account upload are separate states. Skill estate sync reports each one with its receipt.
